known_facts_at_decision_date: IL&FS Group companies defaulted in August and September 2018 on multiple debt instruments including term deposits, short-term deposits, inter-corporate deposits, commercial paper, non-convertible debentures, and other debt obligations
Defaults and associated rating downgrades have created severe pressure across Indian money markets, debt markets, mutual funds, and stock markets
The IL&FS Group's business model involves financing long-gestation infrastructure projects through a complex network of subsidiaries and special purpose vehicles
Asset-liability mismatch is visible: long-dated infrastructure project cash flows are being funded by short-term and medium-term debt instruments
Systemic contagion risk is active: mutual fund redemption pressure, adverse effects on equity and debt markets, and investor confidence in NBFC sector broadly are deteriorating
The group's governance and risk oversight framework has not prevented the accumulation of unsustainable debt relative to project cash flows
Group-level debt quantum and its distribution across subsidiaries and SPVs is not transparently visible to external stakeholders
Multiple credit rating agencies have downgraded IL&FS instruments to below investment grade following the defaults
The liquidity failure is structural — it reflects asset-liability mismatch and inadequate project-level cash flow — not a temporary shortfall
Emergency creditor and stakeholder coordination has not yet been formally established
